original_value: In cognitive radio network, the activities of primary users will cause great influence on the stability of multiple hops routes between cognitive users. In this regard, a joint channel selection and routing protocol, termed as CSRP, is proposed to ensure route stability and reduce route latency between cognitive users. The channel availability based on historical information and the channel switching delay are used as the delay selection criteria to choose the end‐to‐end shortest route which possesses high data delivery probabilities and low delays. Besides, simulation results show that the proposed protocol has a better performance in terms of packet transmission delay and data delivery rate compared with the routing protocols based on channel (TDRP) and based on joint routing and channel allocation (PUB‐JRCA).

result.paraphrase: In cognitive radio networks, primary users can significantly affect the stability of multi-hop routes among cognitive users. To address this, a joint channel-selection and routing protocol called CSRP is proposed to improve route stability and reduce routing latency between cognitive users. Using historical channel availability and channel-switching delay as delay-based selection criteria, it chooses the end-to-end shortest path with high data delivery probability and low delay. Simulation results also indicate that the proposed protocol outperforms the channel-based routing protocol (TDRP) and the joint routing and channel allocation protocol (PUB-JRCA) in packet transmission delay and data delivery rate.
